correctness.rationale: The proof fixes exact supports and Fourier normalization, counts all nine signal-window coefficient products, and proves r_t<=2 from the nontranslate hypothesis. The pair-difference scalar product E equals the number of two-term shifts; each one has at most one Fourier zero because p is prime. Over F2, sign consistency is equivalent to cancelling a full set of double slices at frequency zero. For p>=7 all masks are independent except three-edge nonprogression reflections; in that case multiplying exact complex cancellation equations gives 1=-z^m, impossible for odd p, while two cancellations remain possible. The p=5 exception is handled by a concrete four-zero sign witness and affine transport. The exceptional counts follow from unique progression centers. Exact checker.py exhaustively verifies every unmatched ordered triple pair at p=5,7,11,13; finite enumeration supports but does not prove the infinite result. No unproved auxiliary lemma is needed beyond finite triangle-edge orientation, shown in the proof. A second direct computation in the same standalone checker uses the cyclotomic minimal polynomial to evaluate all 64 sign assignments for each of four representative STFT instances, including a reflected exception, without floating point.

value.rationale: The fixed-input-support STFT uncertainty problem is naturally motivated by sparse radar/time-frequency interpolation. The theorem gives the exact natural invariant min |supp V_g f| for every nontranslated three-point pair at all odd primes, not just a global lower bound. It identifies a mathematical obstruction absent from scalar collision counting: a reflected nonprogression triangle forces one lost potential Fourier cancellation. It completely counts the exceptional ordered pairs, produces explicit sign witnesses, and improves the earlier support-cardinality-only lower bound on the unmatched stratum from 5p-4 to 6p-3 for p>=7. The exception and full fixed-pair formula are structural rather than arbitrary small parameter recomputations.
